overall.sentence: That large-angle twisted van der Waals multilayers energetically favour generalized Halperin (interlayer-correlated, irrational-anyon) liquids over metallic SILC states: no precedent found in the paper's references and 7 searches (5 arXiv, 2 web; 2026-11-22); the earlier work either studies the same class of infinite-layer states in generic stacked 2DEGs or the same twisted-graphite system without fractional states.

assessment.claim: 3: in twisted multilayers, generalized Halperin states replace SILC phases at accessible fields (the headline result)
assessment.note: No precedent found in the paper's references and 7 searches (2026-11-22): 2309.00825 [43] shares the system (alternating twisted graphite) but treats non-interacting 3D Landau levels; Naud et al. [10] share the states but in generic stacked 2DEGs without an energetics study.

assessment.claim: 4: the states have rational charges, irrational braiding and non-foliated order ('a fundamentally new form of fractionalization')
assessment.note: Irrational braiding in infinite-layer generalized Halperin states (question and K-matrix method) is in Naud, Pryadko, Sondhi 2000 [10] and non-foliated order in Ma et al. [7]; new are the specific winning states (3110), (3111) and the finite-layer convergence analysis.

assessment.claim: 6: twisted vdW multilayers as 'the first realistic condensed-matter platform' for non-foliated 3D FQH phases
assessment.note: Realistic platforms for the same infinite-layer states were proposed before (stacked 2DEGs and superlattices in [10], multiple quantum wells with irrational charge in Qiu-Joynt-MacDonald, Supp. ref [20], multilayers in the intermediate-tunneling regime in 0902.0824); the twisted vdW system is the new element.

positioning: The paper combines two lines of earlier work: the theory of infinite-layer generalized Halperin states with irrational braiding and fracton-like order (Naud-Pryadko-Sondhi [10, 11], Ma et al. [7], Qiu-Joynt-MacDonald [32]) and the band structure and quantum Hall experiments of large-angle twisted graphene (refs [24-26], [43]). What it adds, as far as these searches show, is a variational energetics study placing those states in a concrete twisted vdW material and contrasting it with untwisted graphite; no earlier paper found does that. The paper already cites the closest works, so the only items are two wordings ('first realistic platform', 'fundamentally new form of fractionalization') that are stronger than the earlier literature allows. One arXiv query failed repeatedly with HTTP 429 and was replaced by a narrower arXiv query and a web search; a later experiment on trilayer GaAs (2609.26916) is context only.

issues.claim: Twisted vdW multilayers as the first realistic platform
issues.headline: 'First realistic platform' overlooks earlier multilayer and quantum-well proposals
issues.issue: Naud, Pryadko and Sondhi (cond-mat/0006432, cited as [10]) proposed stacked two-dimensional electron systems for the same infinite-layer phases, Qiu, Joynt and MacDonald (Supp. ref. [20]) proposed multiple quantum wells with irrational charge, and Levin and Fisher (0902.0824, not cited) proposed multilayers in the intermediate-tunneling regime. The word 'first' is not contradicted outright, since 'realistic' is a judgment, but a referee who knows these works will read it as overstated.

evidence.quote: Our work suggests that twisted vdW multilayers may provide the first realistic condensed-matter platform for non-foliated topological phases and their associated topological degeneracies.

issues.fix: Drop 'first' and say what makes twisted vdW multilayers more favourable than the earlier quantum-well and superlattice proposals (atomic-scale layer spacing with suppressed tunneling).

edit.before: Our work suggests that twisted vdW multilayers may provide the first realistic condensed-matter platform for non-foliated topological phases and their associated topological degeneracies.
edit.after: Our work suggests that twisted vdW multilayers, which combine atomic-scale layer spacing with suppressed interlayer tunneling, may provide a more favourable condensed-matter platform for non-foliated topological phases and their topological degeneracies than the multilayer quantum wells and superlattices proposed earlier [10, 32].

issues.claim: Irrational braiding as a new form of fractionalization
issues.headline: 'Fundamentally new form of fractionalization' was reported for infinite-layer states in 2000
issues.issue: Rational charges with irrational braiding in infinite-layer Halperin-type states were found by Naud, Pryadko and Sondhi (cond-mat/0006432, cited as [10]) and placed in the fracton framework by Ma et al. [7]. The paper cites both elsewhere, but the Discussion sentence presents the property as this work's finding.

evidence.quote: thereby realizing a fundamentally new form of fractionalization beyond conventional topological order.

issues.fix: Attribute the irrational braiding to [7, 10, 11] in this sentence and state the paper's own contribution: these particular states win energetically and their statistics converge within about 20 layers.

edit.before: thereby realizing a fundamentally new form of fractionalization beyond conventional topological order.
edit.after: thereby realizing in a concrete material the form of fractionalization beyond conventional topological order identified for infinite-layer systems [7, 10, 11].
